notes: The delta number on the slim overlay is written against the right edge of the coloured bar behind it, and that bar had a fixed minimum width narrower than the number. Anything under about a tenth was drawn half on the bar and half on the CHANNELS button beside it. The bar is now measured from the number it has to hold. The Engineer dashboard - the screen the Other device button exists for - had a top bar and an Ask row that were single unwrapping lines, so on a phone they ran off the right and took the Ask button with them; both wrap now, and the lap table scrolls inside its card instead of pushing the page sideways. The manual, the website and the privacy page each had a table or a file-name pattern with no natural place to break, which held the whole page open on a small phone. Behind the scenes: the tool that renders the overlays for testing was dropping any icon drawn straight onto a canvas, so it reported a missing speaker icon on a panel that draws one perfectly well, and it now reads the pixels back from the window; and the test suite read the app's language from your config, so switching GOAT to Spanish failed 45 tests against English text with nothing pointing at why.
